catalyst_system.value: Cu/BN catalysts with unique morphologies (Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, Cu/BN-NP) with 1.0 wt% Cu loading on BN supports
catalyst_system.source_quote: we designed a series of Cu/BN catalysts with unique morphologies for establishing a photothermal ODHP system with high efficiency and selectivity

catalyst_type.source_quote: plasmonic Cu nanoparticles (Cu-NPs) have been loaded onto the BN substrate

active_component.source_quote: The theoretical loading amounts of Cu on the three Cu/BN catalysts were 1.0 wt%

support.value: boron nitride (BN) with different morphologies: nanosheets (BN-NS), nanofibers (BN-NF), and nanoparticles (BN-NP)
support.source_quote: BN nanosheet (BN-NS, 99.9%), BN nanofibers (BN-NF, 99.9%), and BN nanoparticles (BN-NP, 99.9%) were purchased and used as supports

synthesis_method.source_quote: Cu/BN-NS, Cu/BN-NF, and Cu/BN-NP were prepared by wetness impregnation

synthesis_conditions.value: stirring at room temperature at 500 r/min for 10 h, dried at 100°C in air, reduced in 10% H2/N2 mixture at 500°C for 3 h
synthesis_conditions.source_quote: After stirring at room temperature at 500 r/min for 10 h, the samples were evaporated and dried at 100°C in air and reduced in a 10% H2/N2 mixture at 500°C for 3 h

reaction_type.value: photothermal oxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) to propylene
reaction_type.source_quote: Photothermal oxidative dehydrogenation of propane to propylene over Cu/BN catalysts

design_rationale.value: To overcome the challenge of achieving high activity and high propylene selectivity simultaneously in ODHP by utilizing the localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR) effect of Cu nanoparticles to enhance photothermal catalytic performance under visible light irradiation
design_rationale.source_quote: As for the industrial application of ODHP, it is challenging to achieve high activity and high propylene selectivity simultaneously. In this study, to overcome this obstacle, we designed a series of Cu/BN catalysts with unique morphologies for establishing a photothermal ODHP system with high efficiency and selectivity
